entities.name: LinkedIn
entities.how_described: 本集主讲人所在的公司,拥有超过 1,000 个仓库、数千个微服务和大量自建基础设施,他们为编码智能体搭建了 Contextual Agent Playbooks and Tools 系统让 AI 在企业内真正可用

evidence.quote: But yeah, my name is Ajay, and I am a software engineer at LinkedIn.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Today I'm going to be talking about how we are doing context engineering to improve the performance of coding agents at LinkedIn.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So this is how teams at LinkedIn are using coding agents as effective coworkers with deep understanding of LinkedIn's internal systems and code to help the teams be really productive.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And this is possible because of a system that we built called Contextual Agent Playbooks and Tools at LinkedIn.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So just like any other company, even at LinkedIn, we wanted to use the coding agents for our engineers and everyone to be really productive with the AI.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So we started giving these coding agents to all of the engineers, and the problem was the coding agents doesn't really, or the wipe coding doesn't really work in a large enterprise like LinkedIn.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So they don't have the context of how we are mature code bases at LinkedIn or our internal frameworks, our internal systems.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: To understand the problem, to get more perspective, so if you look at the LinkedIn stack, we have over 1,000 repos which make up thousands of microservices and apps.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: We have our own configuration management system, which is purely internal to LinkedIn and coding agents doesn't have any idea about them.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: How can we make any coding agent like Cursor or Claude Code or GitHub Copilot understand our LinkedIn's internal system so well that they can ship the code that our engineers can trust?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So we have a pretty sophisticated CodeSearch system at LinkedIn where engineers can go and search for code.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And the agent can use the code search tools to figure out the right examples of how we do things at LinkedIn and use that to give you an answer and also implement it based on its findings.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: For example, if the engineer goes and asks, how do I set up an Airflow DAG at LinkedIn, the agent will first decide, okay, so I have a playbook for creating that specific task, and it will use that first, uses that playbook to get the information, and then it calls the necessary, follows that instructions and calls the relevant tools to get the job done.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Mainly because now anyone at LinkedIn can go ahead and create, set up a playbook and check it into a repository and make it available for everyone else at LinkedIn.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So this particular system, we have one local MCP server, and it is automatically installed on all of the LinkedIn laptops by default.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So if you join LinkedIn and you get a laptop, it is pre-installed, and any updates to the MCP server or the playbooks of the tools, it automatically gets updated every one hour on all the laptops.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: In a large enterprise like LinkedIn, it's not just enough to give all of the engineers all the latest and greatest tools and models.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Thank you for attending, and feel free to connect with me on LinkedIn.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

entities.name: MCP

evidence.quote: So in early 2025, last year, so Anthropic released MCP and it quickly became the industry standard for building tools to the agents.

evidence.quote: We leveraged that and pretty early on, we built our own internal MCP.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So we made that available to the coding agents via MCP.

evidence.quote: So every tool that we added to our internal MCP, it created more value.

evidence.quote: So we built a system, we invented a system in early 2025 called as Playbooks, where we not only provide the tools to the agents via MCP, we also allow the agents to access these instructions and prompts via MCP.

evidence.quote: And Playbooks are a little bit more nuanced because it helps us seamlessly capture all of the organizational context and service via MCP without much of a setup.

entities.name: Playbooks
entities.how_described: LinkedIn 2025 年初发明的系统:把指令和提示词本身做成 MCP 上的资源,像普通工具一样被智能体调用,从而捕获隐性知识;原则是自包含、拆小再引用,且让智能体使用后自己提 PR 更新,形成自我学习飞轮

evidence.quote: And this is possible because of a system that we built called Contextual Agent Playbooks and Tools at LinkedIn.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So we built a system, we invented a system in early 2025 called as Playbooks, where we not only provide the tools to the agents via MCP, we also allow the agents to access these instructions and prompts via MCP.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: We call it Playbooks.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So as people started creating more playbooks, so we wanted, so this is one of two foundational principles we want everyone to follow when creating a playbook.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And the second most important one is to break a big playbook into multiple smaller playbooks.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And reference those smaller playbooks from a bigger playbook.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So if you have a small self-contained playbooks, it can be used from multiple, referenced from multiple playbooks.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Context, which means the agent, only when it needs to read a smaller playbook, instead of reading the entire, all of the playbooks at once, it can progressively go and read the playbooks as it wants.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So playbooks are very similar to skills, but we developed this entire system around playbooks even before skills was a thing.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And Playbooks are a little bit more nuanced because it helps us seamlessly capture all of the organizational context and service via MCP without much of a setup.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And another cool thing about this Playbooks is the self-improving loop.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So you have engineers creating these playbooks and checking into the repository.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And we also encourage the agents to figure out how to improve the playbook and use that context to update the playbooks, check out the repository and update the playbooks and create a PR.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And once it gets approved, the playbooks gets updated.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So if you join LinkedIn and you get a laptop, it is pre-installed, and any updates to the MCP server or the playbooks of the tools, it automatically gets updated every one hour on all the laptops.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And we have a concept of two local playbooks and central playbooks, which means, so central playbooks are the playbooks which are cross-cutting in nature, right?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So you have, these playbooks apply for multiple repositories, not just one code repository.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And then you have local playbooks.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: These are the playbooks which are very specific to your code repository, and you can just have them checked in with your repo, and only when the coding agents are working in your repo, those playbooks will be automatically picked up.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So this helps us scale the local playbooks which are very specific to repo without having to worry about changing the central repository.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00
